_comment: agentx_glm52, but with the baseline reproduced from scratch instead of adopted from a receipt. Identical to config/agentx_glm52.json except for stages.baseline. Use this when the question is whether *this machine* can still hit CI run 34783501425 -- before a long campaign, after a node or image change, or when a previous baseline and the CI figure disagree. It costs an hour on eight GPUs; agentx_glm52.json costs nothing and reuses a number that was already reproduced to within 0.07%.

ci._note_band: 0.5% is wide enough to absorb run-to-run noise on this workload and narrow enough to catch a dropped pin. For scale: the local reproduction landed 0.07% from CI, while the node-local pristine leg sits 0.12% below the receipt.

trace_corpus._note: A named public-dataset loader, not a file. The harness picks it from MODEL_PREFIX=glm5.2; it is pinned here so a change in that default shows up as a mismatch rather than as unexplained drift. The loader name selects the corpus generation, and 062126 and 061526 have different prompt-length mixes.

pins._note_benchmark_id: Deliberately null: there is no safe default. The AgentX cache-bust marker embeds the AIPerf benchmark id, so the id IS the KV keyspace -- reusing one starts the run on warmed prefixes and measures high with nothing in the output saying so. Set a fresh id per run; preflight refuses any id already in runs/.benchmark_id_ledger.json.
pins._note_revision: The weights are pinned by revision rather than by wiping the weights cache: emptying HF_HOME re-downloads tens of gigabytes and can change what is served underneath the run.

cpu._note_affinity: 0, not 1. sglang derives per-rank masks from the full topology, so under a restricted cpuset it binds to CPUs the cgroup then denies. This node has 118 physical cores over 2 sockets (236 logical); if the run is granted the whole node, 1 is correct -- but it must then be 1 in every arm compared against it.

isolation._note_mounts: Bind mounts rather than plain -e, because tools/environment.sh exports these three variables itself and an -e pin would lose to it. A fresh empty directory under this run's out/ is mounted onto each path the harness names, so the harness's own export lands cold. The shared cache tree is shadowed, never emptied -- other runs out of that directory are untouched.
isolation._note_hf: HF_HUB_CACHE and the dataset mmap cache are intentionally absent: they hold weights and corpus, which must be warm and pinned, not cold.

params._note_env_map: Empty on purpose. The harness sets seed, benchmark id and cache-bust itself through build_replay_cmd; passing a second set of variables would mean two sources of truth for the same pin. The proof pass reads back what the client actually recorded, so an unset pin surfaces as a mismatch rather than as silence.

harness._note: The site's own CI harness is driven rather than reimplemented, so what is reproduced stays what was measured. It refuses to overwrite an existing RESULT_DIR, so run_tag must be new -- it defaults to the benchmark_id, which preflight has already proven unused.

params.selection: per-phase Top 5 AND overall GPU-time share > 3%

params._note_reference: null, so the A/B reference is this config's own freshly reproduced baseline rather than a receipt from another node. That is the point of running ci-run-replay: both arms are measured on this machine, by this harness, against the same corpus.
